# SeaCommons funding brief

Public proposal, 3 October 2026. Proposed activities require a funding agreement.

## Purpose

SeaCommons is open-source maritime research infrastructure. It connects
fragmented observations into traceable case records for humanitarian incidents
and maritime investigations. Source lineage, location precision and uncertainty
remain visible so readers can inspect and challenge an interpretation.

The intended users are humanitarian organisations, investigative researchers
and public-interest institutions. These are intended audiences, not a claim of
existing adoption. The current funding proposition is a scoped research pilot.

## Current evidence and limits

The repository contains incident ingestion and correlation code, public Live
and archive interfaces, evidence documentation and automated checks. Readers
can inspect the code and methods. Repository capability is distinct from current
deployment health, continuous geographic coverage and validated user benefit.

- [Repository](https://github.com/suezcanalxyz/seacommons)
- [Methods and limits](https://seacommons.org/docs)
- [Deployment status](https://seacommons.org/status)
- [Live surface](https://live.seacommons.org)
- [Archive surface](https://play.seacommons.org)

Public archive totals describe records, not people assisted, independently
verified incidents or partner adoption. Source availability and coverage require
measurement. AIS gaps are indicators requiring review. Repeated reports can
share one underlying source. Models do not establish a verified location.

## Proposed pilot

Six months from an agreed start, with a bounded geography and case sample.

| Period | Activity | Deliverable and review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–2 | Audit deployment health and source coverage. Agree review conditions and the evaluation protocol. | Coverage report, baseline dataset and signed evaluation scope. Review before case validation. |
| Months 3–4 | Review selected humanitarian and maritime cases. Record unsupported associations, corrections and analyst effort. | Case sample with source lineage, uncertainty and correction log. Review against the agreed protocol. |
| Months 5–6 | Evaluate against the baseline and document operational requirements. | Evaluation report, operating runbook and costed continuation proposal. Decision on continued support. |

The proposal does not imply a committed start date, participating organisation,
funding award or guaranteed operational outcome.

## Evaluation

| Measure | Method |
| --- | --- |
| Source availability | Compare received updates with the expected source schedule, by geography. Publish denominators, outages and coverage gaps. |
| Evidence traceability | Measure the share of reviewed cases with inspectable source lineage, location precision and transformation history. |
| Review quality | Record unsupported associations and corrections in a documented sample. Separate independent corroboration from repeated reports. |
| Research usefulness | Compare time to assemble a case record with an agreed baseline workflow and collect participant assessments. |

Before evaluation, participants must agree sample selection, review roles,
baselines and acceptance thresholds. Case volume alone cannot establish impact.

## Use of funds and budget method

Support would cover reliable infrastructure, evidence validation and partner use
with continued maintenance. A scoped budget must show the following cost drivers.

| Budget line | Cost basis | Evidence of delivery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engineering | Agreed days × agreed rate | Deployment recovery, integration work and reviewed releases |
| Data and source access | Provider quotes, licence conditions and agreed geography | Source register and coverage report |
| Hosting and reliability | Infrastructure quotes for the pilot period, storage and backups | Monitoring report and recovery exercise |
| Case review | Agreed review hours × agreed rate | Reviewed sample and correction log |
| Participation and onboarding | Agreed facilitation effort and eligible expenses | Documented feedback and training materials |
| Continued maintenance | Explicitly costed support period and responsibility | Runbook and continuation proposal |

The total funding amount remains unset until these inputs are confirmed.
Grant and sponsor support may fund defined deliverables. An equity proposition
would additionally require a verified legal entity, business model, financial
forecast and proposed terms. None is implied by this brief.

## Delivery and governance

SeaCommons is developed by suezcanal.xyz. Matteo Messina leads the proposed
technical delivery. A pilot agreement must name the accountable contracting
entity and assign case review, participant coordination and maintenance roles.
No additional staff or institutional endorsement is implied.

Sensitive operational data stays outside public case projections. Review rules
must specify data access, retention, publication and correction. AGPL-3.0
licensing allows inspection of the software. SeaCommons is research
infrastructure and does not replace emergency coordination authorities.

## Next decision

Agree the research geography and sample, participant roles, data access,
evaluation criteria and a costed delivery plan. Then set the funding amount and
milestone conditions. Contact: research@seacommons.org.
